narrative:
The model predicts you have a 37% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to help you graduate.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. By far the strongest factor is that you have already failed three classes in the past. Among students who passed, the average number of previous failures is zero, so this history strongly pushes the model toward expecting you will fail again.

Two other factors pulled the prediction in the opposite direction, making failure less likely than it otherwise would have been. First, you did not attend nursery school; most students who passed (79%) did attend, so your background here actually helped the model’s confidence that you can still succeed. Second, you report having only a low amount of free time after school. This is relatively uncommon among students who passed and worked in your favor, as it suggests you may have fewer distractions.

Even with these positive signals, your past academic failures outweighed them. To improve, focus immediately on catching up in the subjects you have previously failed. Talk to your teachers about targeted support, create a realistic study schedule, and reduce weekend socializing if possible. Taking the remedial courses seriously is the clearest step you can take right now to raise your chances of passing. (248 words)
